On 2023-05-21, the user said they could not wait to try making a classic French omelette; they had not yet said they had made one.

A classic French omelette recipe discussed on 2023-05-21 uses 2–3 eggs, a pinch of salt, 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, and optionally 1 tablespoon finely chopped herbs. Whisk eggs and salt until combined; heat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, melt and swirl the butter without browning it, pour in the eggs, spread them, and cook about 30 seconds until they begin to set. Fold both sides toward the center, slide onto a plate, and garnish with herbs if desired.

Tips given for a light, fluffy French omelette: whisk the eggs until frothy and fully combined; use a nonstick skillet; cook over medium-high heat without overcooking; keep fillings light; fold gently without pressing; and serve immediately.

Suggested French omelette fillings and combinations included Swiss, cheddar, or Gruyere; sautéed ham; sautéed mushrooms; spinach with sautéed onions and garlic; cooked tomatoes; parsley, thyme, or chives; ham and cheese; mushrooms and cheese; spinach and feta; tomato and basil; and smoked salmon with dill. For the article’s author description, the user requested that the conclusion state: the user is a solicitor and construction lawyer with more than 10 years’ experience specialising in construction law; regularly advises homeowners and builders about contractual and legal rights; represents homeowners and builders in NSW, Australia, and all courts of competent jurisdiction; has advised homeowners, builders, and contractors about clause 23 of the HIA NSW Lump Sum Contract, their contract rights, risks, and obligations; and has negotiated and amended contracts to reflect their intentions.
